fit: permitted spearmint and fatigue testimonials in a lifestyle program
assessment: The protocol explicitly permits spearmint. Fatigue testimonials occur in other diagnoses, with no verified fresh spearmint use or Parkinson-specific fatigue estimate.

fit: 1908 account of drowsiness and stupor in earlier nutmeg poison cases
assessment: Cushny summarized Wallace’s cases and adverse poison effects. This is historical evidence of acute toxicity rather than a separate ordinary-serving trial.

fit: suspected accidental excessive nutmeg in food and next-morning drowsiness
assessment: The patient reported adding more ground spice than intended and also drank alcohol. Drowsiness arose with other poisoning symptoms. No ordinary-serving or Parkinson estimate.

fit: nutmeg fruit syrup and pre/post alertness task
assessment: Precision moved lower and response time difference was inconclusive. The material was fruit syrup, with no verified ground seed, control group or measured daytime sleepiness.

fit: permitted dill and fatigue testimonials in a lifestyle program
assessment: Dill weed is listed. Non-Parkinson testimonies describe fatigue changes without individual dried-dill intake or separate effects.

fit: pooled corn-or-soy oil placebo and comparative fall events in Alzheimer dementia
assessment: Falls were reported in 33 of 164 pooled placebo participants and 42 of 238 DHA participants (p=.60). The aggregate does not identify recipients of corn versus soy, oil refining or Parkinson results.

fit: canola spread comparator with measured TOVA in children
assessment: Table 5 gives −0.45 ± 2.51, within-arm p=.418. The abstract gives −0.42. Contrasts compare fatty-acid formulations without a verified refined-oil or Parkinson effect.

fit: rapeseed bread crossover and objective selective attention
assessment: Selective attention and working memory differences were inconclusive. Lipid-free bread was faster for psychomotor response time than all lipid meals. This is distinct from a selective attention effect.

fit: rapeseed-containing comparator in a childhood EPA trial
assessment: Teacher-rated inattention favored EPA, while total Conners scores were inconclusive. No oil-only or verified refined canola effect.

fit: red spinach extract and Stroop outcomes in resistance-trained men
assessment: The crossover found no clear Stroop difference. The product was an extract and is distinct from cooked common spinach in Parkinson disease.

fit: optional spinach intake and objective postpartum attention
assessment: Spinach entries were documented in both intervention groups and the MANT accuracy interaction was significant. The intervention varied a bundle of foods without a cooking or spinach-specific contrast.

fit: mixed evening meal with lentils and next-morning Epworth sleepiness
assessment: The 20-participant comparison found no clear Epworth difference (p=.45). Ingredients and calories changed together, and canned lentil and Parkinson effects were unmeasured.

fit: pea protein breakfast and exploratory cognition reporting
assessment: The registry reports actual enrollment of 40 and no posted results. The likely companion reports food intake only, with executive results still open.
